concepts.title: Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition
concepts.definition: Multiplying a number by a sum gives the same result as multiplying by each addend separately and adding the products: a times (b + c) equals a times b plus a times c; an area rectangle split into two blocks shows the identity, and expanding from either bracket side gives the same terms.
concepts.formula: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c
concepts.key_idea: Multiplication distributes across the bracket: 23 x (27 + 1) = 23 x 27 + 23.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp106.txt lines 14-60 (properties, area model), 60-90 (expansion from either side)

solution_steps.explain: Write a times the bracket as the two separate products a b and a c.
A rectangle a by (b + c) splits into an a by b block and an a by c block of the same total area.
Substituting values such as a = 23, b = 27, c = 1 confirms both sides agree.

concepts.title: How Products Increase When Factors Grow
concepts.definition: Increasing the two factors of a product ab by 1 each adds exactly a + b + 1 to the product, since (a + 1)(b + 1) expands to ab + b + a + 1; raising one factor by m and the other by n adds an + bm + mn, the area of the new L-shaped border of rectangles.
concepts.formula: increase = a * n + b * m + m * n
concepts.key_idea: (23 + 1)(27 + 1) = 23 x 27 + 27 + 23 + 1: the growth is the frame around the ab block.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp106.txt lines 90-200 (increments by 1), 185-200 (increase by m and n, Identity 1)

solution_steps.explain: (a + m)(b + n) distributes into ab plus three border products.
The increase is the new product minus ab, which equals an + bm + mn.

concepts.title: Square of a Sum (Identity 1A)
concepts.definition: Squaring a two-term sum gives the square of each term plus twice their product: (a + b) squared equals a squared + 2ab + b squared; a 65 by 65 square splits into a 60-square, a 5-square and two 60 by 5 rectangles, so 65 squared = 3600 + 25 + 600 = 4225.
concepts.formula: value = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b
concepts.key_idea: Split big squares into easy parts: (60 + 5) squared = 60 squared + 2 x 60 x 5 + 5 squared.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp106.txt lines 608-680 (square of sum, 652 example, Identity 1A)

solution_steps.explain: Compute a squared and b squared separately.

concepts.title: Square of a Difference (Identity 1B)
concepts.definition: Squaring a difference keeps the two squares but removes twice the product: (a - b) squared equals a squared - 2ab + b squared; geometrically, the 55-square inside a 60-square loses two 60 by 5 strips and gains back the overlapping 5-square, giving 3025.
concepts.formula: value = a * a - 2 * a * b + b * b
concepts.key_idea: (60 - 5) squared = 3600 - 300 - 300 + 25 = 3025: subtract both strips, add back the overlap.

concepts.title: Sum Times Difference (Identity 1C)
concepts.definition: Multiplying a sum by the matching difference cancels the middle terms and leaves a difference of squares: (a + b)(a - b) equals a squared minus b squared; this explains patterns like 9 x 9 - 1 x 1 = 10 x 8 and gives shortcuts such as 98 x 102 = 10000 - 4.
concepts.key_idea: 98 x 102 = 100 squared - 2 squared = 9996: pair the factors around a common centre.

concepts.title: Twice the Sum of Squares Pattern
concepts.definition: Adding the two square identities cancels the cross terms and yields twice the sum of squares: (a + b) squared + (a - b) squared equals 2(a squared + b squared), which explains the number pattern 2(5 squared + 6 squared) = 11 squared + 1 squared.
concepts.key_idea: Sum and difference squares together double the plain sum of squares.

solution_steps.explain: List a squared + 2ab + b squared and a squared - 2ab + b squared.
The 2ab and minus 2ab cancel, the squares double.
The total is 2(a squared + b squared), proving the observed pattern always holds.
